scenario: AITA for not painting my step father in a family picture? | I wanted to do something nice for my mom for her birthday, so I decided to paint her a picture. I oil paint as a hobby. I made a really sweet picture, I don’t want to post it here because it’s personal, but it was a picture of my mom smiling and holding my younger brother, as my dad pushed me on the swing in the background. It took me like 6 weeks or so to finish this painting. I gave it to my mom, and she cried she loved it. My parents aren’t together anymore but they were good friends until my mom met my step dad. First thing he said when she opened the painting was, “well, where am I?” This pissed me off and I ignored it but he kept going, saying if I needed a reference picture I could have asked him, and calling me rude and “exclusionary” because he’s a part of the family too and kept going on and on. I told him I didn’t paint him because I can’t stand to look at his face for that long. He slammed the table like a petulant child and stormed out. My mom scolded me for being rude, and asked me to apologize for not putting him in the painting. WHAT? I still haven’t said a word to this man, it’s been about three weeks. My mom also hasn’t hung the picture up which really hurts my feelings. AITA?

Scenario:
AITA for not painting my step father in a family picture? | I wanted to do something nice for my mom for her birthday, so I decided to paint her a picture. I oil paint as a hobby. I made a really sweet picture, I don’t want to post it here because it’s personal, but it was a picture of my mom smiling and holding my younger brother, as my dad pushed me on the swing in the background. It took me like 6 weeks or so to finish this painting. I gave it to my mom, and she cried she loved it. My parents aren’t together anymore but they were good friends until my mom met my step dad. First thing he said when she opened the painting was, “well, where am I?” This pissed me off and I ignored it but he kept going, saying if I needed a reference picture I could have asked him, and calling me rude and “exclusionary” because he’s a part of the family too and kept going on and on. I told him I didn’t paint him because I can’t stand to look at his face for that long. He slammed the table like a petulant child and stormed out. My mom scolded me for being rude, and asked me to apologize for not putting him in the painting. WHAT? I still haven’t said a word to this man, it’s been about three weeks. My mom also hasn’t hung the picture up which really hurts my feelings. AITA?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: **0 (Not the Asshole)** **Here's why:** ### 1️️ **The painting was a personal gift for your biological mother** - You explicitly created it *for her birthday*. It was never intended to be a " family" portrait inclusive of everyone in the household. - The scene you described (mom, your biological dad, and your younger brother) reflects *your* family unit at the time the memory was created. Stepfather wasn’t part of that dynamic, and **you have no obligation to include him in a deeply personal artwork that doesn’t represent his role in your life**. ### 2️️ **Stepfather overstepped boundaries** - His reaction ("*where am I?*" immediately after seeing it, calling you "exclusionary," and demanding a reference photo) was entitled and inappropriate. - **He is not the recipient of the gift**—your mom is. His entitlement to dictate the content of a gift *she* chose to receive is a violation of boundaries. - His "slamming the table like a petulant child" shows emotional immaturity, not legitimate concern. ### 3️️ **Your reason for exclusion is valid** - You stated: "*I can’t stand to look at his face for that long.*" This implies a history of trauma, conflict, or deep emotional discomfort with him. **Forcing yourself to include someone you actively cannot tolerate in a labor-intensive, emotionally vulnerable project is unreasonable and potentially harmful**. - Art is personal expression. You have the right to exclude people who don’t belong in the narrative you’re creating. ### 4️️ **Your mom’s reaction is concerning (but doesn’t make *you* wrong)** - Her scolding you and not hanging the painting *does* hurt your feelings, but ** her behavior doesn’t change the fact that you acted appropriately**. - A healthy parent would prioritize their child’s emotional well-being over stepfather’s demands. Her response suggests she’s prioritizing stepfather’s ego over your effort and boundaries, which is unfair—but ** that’s on her, not you**. ### 💡 **Key takeaway** - **Stepfather is the one who should apologize** for overstepping. - **You did nothing wrong** by creating a meaningful gift for your mom that reflects *your* truth. - If stepfather genuinely cares about " family," he’d respect your boundaries instead of demanding inclusion in a project that doesn’t involve him. **Do not apologize**. This is about your right to set boundaries and create art that authent reflects your experience. If your mom truly loves you, she’ll eventually recognize that her reaction was unfair. 💛 *(Note: If stepfather’s behavior has historically been abusive or toxic, your exclusion is not only justified but necessary for your safety and mental health.)*
